sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A small species, with the head and abdomen almost hairless. The soldier has an orange red-brown head, a darkest rostrum and orange yellow antennae; the posterior 2/3 of the head is spherical in dorsal view, and the rostrum is very long, slightly longer than 2/3 of the rest of the head, broader at the base and evenly tapering to a sharp point; antennae 13-segmented; mandibles usually with a pointed tooth. The alate is not recorded in the original. For comparison between species the original says only "See E. apiocephalus" and gives no further account under this species.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
A small species, with the head and abdomen almost hairless. Head orange red-brown, rostrum darkest, antennae orange yellow. The posterior 2/3 of the head spherical in dorsal view; rostrum very long, slightly longer than 2/3 of the rest of the head, broader at the base and evenly tapering to a sharp point. The dorsum of the head is almost straight in lateral view, or the rostrum is slightly turned upwards. Antennae 13-segmented; segment 1 long and slender; segment 2 about half of segment 1 and distinctly narrower, cylindrical; segment 3 about as long as segment 2 but narrower; segment 4 much shorter than segments 3 and 5; segments 6—9 about equal in length, longer than segment 5; segments 10—12 equal in length, shorter than segment 13; segment 13 about as long as segment 3 and distinctly shorter than segment 12. Mandibles usually with a pointed tooth.
Measurements: body length 3.00—3.75 mm; head length (to apex of rostrum) 1.32—1.52 mm; head width 0.66—0.80 mm; pronotum width 0.38—0.44 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text:
Head orange, widest in front, narrowing towards the hemispherical posterior margin. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 2 distinctly longer than segment 3; segment 4 the shortest of all. Postclypeus about as long as wide.
Measurements: body length 3.75—4.00 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.24 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.70 mm; head width 0.95 mm.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the original gives it as Eutermes comatus sp. nov., with the type locality Magnetic Island (Qld). The alate is recorded as 'Not known' in the original, so that section is not included. Under Affinities the original says only 'See E. apiocephalus' and does not develop the comparison under this species. OCR misreadings: 'hase'='base', 'hent up'='bent up', 'pro-notum' broken across lines as pronotum, '3-75'='3.75', 'Eamiterrwes'='Hamitermes', 'Miorocerotermes'='Microcerotermes', 'apiooephalus'='apiocephalus'.
